projects.title: EchoTales
projects.description: Turns a translated web novel into a full-cast audiobook and manga-style panels. Underneath is a bitemporal narrative knowledge graph that tracks every character's aliases, attributes and relationships across a whole volume, so it can say who a name refers to at any point in the story, even when titles change hands, identities are faked and later retracted, or one chapter mixes present action with flashbacks. Voice casting, prosody, reference sheets and panel casting all read from that one query, and decisions it is unsure of go to a review queue whose size is reported as a metric. Built on Reverend Insanity Vol. 1 (199 chapters, about 21,000 audiobook spans), with spot checks on Lord of the Mysteries and Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint. It started as a DevJams finalist project.

projects.title: ComputeHive
projects.description: A self-hosted distributed task runner. Point it at a directory and it builds a container image, picks the best available machine, runs the job in a locked-down sandbox and returns the result. Workers can be servers or volunteers' laptops behind NAT, since they pull work over an outbound gRPC connection. The guarantees are tested rather than assumed: an atomic Lua queue in Redis gives each job to exactly one worker, a dead worker's jobs are requeued in under 15 seconds, per-attempt lease tokens stop a presumed-dead worker from committing a stale result, and a 1,000-job run with random worker kills loses nothing and commits nothing twice. A contributor's machine is never pushed past 90% of its RAM, CPU or disk. It ships with a CLI, a Tauri desktop app and Prometheus and Grafana dashboards.

projects.title: Catalyst (LabTutor)
projects.description: A learning-support system for VIT's Applied Chemistry Lab (BACHY105), built alongside a research paper on LLMs in undergraduate chemistry education. It catches mistakes while the student is still doing the experiment instead of days later at grading. No language model decides anything: every pass/fail verdict, expected value and error diagnosis is computed by deterministic Python from the lab manual's formulas, so a demonstrator can reproduce any diagnosis by hand, and models only phrase conclusions already reached. Socratic mode checks each step against the student's own readings with a hint ladder that never names the number, and the final answer is kept out of every model's context by data minimisation rather than by asking a model to keep a secret. It is sized for 70 concurrent students.

projects.title: StoryTrace & SSR-Bench V2
projects.description: An agentic continuity checker for screenplays and novels, paired with a research benchmark. StoryTrace turns documents into a temporal model of story state in ClickHouse (character presence, location, prop possession across every scene), finds suspicious state transitions with SQL window functions, and hands each one to an investigation agent that queries the database through ClickHouse MCP tools and returns a verdict with evidence. Re-uploading a revised draft compares its conflicts against the earlier version. SSR-Bench V2 measures how well LLMs revise story state after a single pivot event, using leak-free matched story pairs: a story-blind attacker scores 0.000 pair-both, while the replay oracle scores 1.000.

projects.title: Shadow-Code
projects.description: Java migration intelligence, built in a four-person team and Track Winner at DevSoc (CodeChef VIT, 1,200+ participants). It parses a Java repository into an AST, builds a dependency graph with cycle detection, and scores every file by complexity, coupling, blast radius and risky patterns on a D3 force-directed risk map. Before converting a file to Go, Kotlin or TypeScript with Gemini, it gives a SAFE, REVIEW or RISKY verdict, then shows the original and converted code side by side.

projects.title: METIS-X
projects.description: A cache-conscious, header-only C++ symbol table for embedded toolchains and language runtimes, written up as an IEEE-format paper. Prefix compression cut RAM by 20% but made p95 lookup latency 2.4x worse, so I redesigned the table around 32-byte cache-line inline slots, Robin Hood hashing and recyclable scope arenas. On Zephyr RTOS's 228k symbols it uses 40.2% less RAM with 45.7% lower p95 lookup latency, and the ablation shows an 89.1% memory reduction against a heap-allocating baseline. A differential fuzzing suite checks it against the earlier implementations.

projects.title: OS-Tutor
projects.description: A Socratic tutor for operating systems that answers only from the course's own lecture decks, OSTEP chapters and lab handouts, shows its sources, then asks one short question to check the student understood, at ELI5, undergrad or exam-prep depth. The repo also holds a research project on whether executable reasoning benchmarks are identifiable when the gold reference is one of many valid solutions. Across 1,152 model outputs on 24 OS tasks and 50,000 Monte Carlo draws, changing only the reference flipped pairwise model winners in 18.61% of draws, and exact-match scoring recovered the true model ranking only 2.86% of the time.

projects.title: Verity
projects.description: A financial-crime analyst workspace built for a hackathon. Card-fraud alerts and ledger account risk feed one case queue, scored by three engines: a fraud model with SHAP explanations and split-conformal risk intervals, ledger anomaly detection, and FATF typology rules for structuring, round-tripping and rapid layering. A hand-rolled tool-calling agent with a grounding filter investigates each case, and the analyst can question it about its own reasoning live. Four services share JSON-schema contracts, kept consistent by an 80-test suite.

projects.title: Chapter Recruitment Platform
projects.description: ACM-VIT's recruitment system, which I co-led. Applicants move through a 3-stage pipeline across 5 domains, with role-based access, multi-stage candidate evaluation and automatic interview scheduling. It processed 1,100+ applications and increased chapter membership by 40%.

projects.title: Cryptic Hunt Backend
projects.description: The backend for ACM-VIT's Cryptic Hunt, a 36-hour live event played through an Android app. I refactored a monolithic legacy codebase into Go microservices on a normalized PostgreSQL schema and built a real-time admin dashboard for live monitoring. It served 600+ concurrent users and 70,000+ API requests with zero downtime.

projects.title: Proteus
projects.description: Drift-aware intrusion detection for software-defined networks. A Random Forest scores flows; when a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test flags drift, a conditional WGAN-GP generates samples of the affected classes, an MMD fidelity gate filters them, and a bounded-memory classifier retrains. A daemon packages each candidate as a hashed release, hot-swaps it and rolls back on canary failure, while a Ryu controller feeds live OpenFlow statistics. I then tested whether the augmentation actually helps under a leak-free, preregistered protocol. It did not in the tested regime, so I retracted my earlier headline result and wrote up the negative finding in a paper.

projects.title: FormSpace
projects.description: A Google Forms-style platform for teams, with a visual workflow layer. Forms are built on a drag-and-drop canvas from eight question types, and sections wire into branching paths that route respondents on nested AND/OR conditions over their answers. Workspaces have a six-level role hierarchy, email invites and per-form sharing; responses can be filtered, analysed and exported to Excel, with file uploads through presigned S3 URLs.

projects.title: Load & Stability Analyzer
projects.description: A load-testing tool for HTTP APIs. A Go worker pool fires bounded concurrent requests, with an optional ramp-up of one worker per second, and the run comes back as latency percentiles, a weighted stability score (error rate, P95 latency, retry amplification and throughput) and a collapse flag when the error rate passes 20% or P95 exceeds five times the average latency. It also estimates the cloud cost of the run.
